newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Some basis bids strengthen.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Some basis bids strengthen.

text.p: Some basis bids for hard red winter wheat at interior and Gulf locations strengthened further, grain merchandisers said Monday.

Meanwhile, dealers in Kansas and Oklahoma expressed optimism over planting conditions for HRW wheat after several inches of rain fell over the weekend. One northeast Oklahoma dealer said his region received more than three inches of rain and Kansas dealers reported similar weather.
"It looks like wheat will get off to a great start if it dries up like they say it's supposed to this week," a south central Kansas dealer said.
But dealers said the rains, while beneficial for wheat, were not conducive for fall harvest activities.
"Most people were hoping to get a lot of (harvest) work done this weekend. They weren't able to," the dealer said.
Another central Kansas dealer reported taking five cents per bushel protection on wheat, but most other dealers said they were not taking any protection.
Basis values are quoted against KCBT wheat, cash dollars/bu.
